paragraphs.source_en: So it appears that the center was at least planning on formatting this realm according to its own templates.65 Somehow the imperial system also tamed the fractious and autonomist tendencies of the Armenian nobility, who caused little trouble during the period of Roman sovereignty. Rather, they reached for new opportunities. The nobleman Grigor of the Pahlavuni family surrendered his lands to the empire in exchange for others in Edessa, along with titles. He was made doux of Vaspurakan in the early 1050s, although he did not accept Chalcedon.66 This was a notable accommodation on the part of Constantinople: while a parallel Chalcedonian Church was gradually being set up in Roman Armenia, state offices were given to Armenian noblemen who did not subscribe to Roman Orthodoxy, unlike the Syrians, who were not given offices.
